restoration_note: This short chapter states the foundational dualism: two essences (Light=Divine love-and-wisdom; Darkness=proprium/self-love-and-falsity) exist 'from the beginning,' expressed in three correspondential pairs (Light/Darkness, beautiful/bitter, life/death), with the redemptive operation being ⲡⲱⲣⲭ — separating beautiful from Darkness. Restorations are tightly constrained: {1} by trace ⲡ_ⲛⲉ + dualistic catalogue (ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ → ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ); {2} by the parallel formula 'X ⲙⲛ̄ Y' where ⲡⲙⲟⲩ on the next line demands its life-counterpart (ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄); {0} as the predicate copula ⲛⲉ that introduces the catalogue. No portion is too damaged to fill — the formula and the spiritual arc both bind every slot.

restorations.basis: Coptic predicate copula ⲛⲉ introducing the enumeration: 'Two substances existing from the beginning ARE: the Light and the Darkness...' The editor's note ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈/'Lig-' actually belongs to gap {1} (ⲡ_ⲛⲉ trace); {0} stands as the small connector before ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ. Grammatically required by the nominal sentence pattern X ⲛⲉ A ⲙⲛ̄ B.

Trace ⲡ{1}|ⲛⲉ at line break = ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ 'the Light' — the standard first member of the Light/Darkness dualistic catalogue (lexicon: ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ = wisdom/Divine Truth). Editor's restoration ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈/'Lig-' confirms. The English 'Light' is split across the line break.

restorations.basis: ⲡⲉⲧⲥⲁ{2} completes to ⲡⲉⲧⲥⲁϣⲉ 'the bitter one' (lexicon: ⲥⲓϣⲉ/ⲥⲁϣⲉ = quality of falsity-from-evil). The reading explicitly names three pairs (Light/Darkness, beautiful/bitter, life/death), and the next line gives only ⲡⲙⲟⲩ 'the death' — which requires its life-counterpart ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄ (Lycopolitan for ⲱⲛϩ̄, attested across the lexicon's compounds: ⲧⲙⲉⲩ ⲙ̄ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄, ⲡⲡⲛⲁ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄). The conjunctive ⲙⲛ̄...ⲙⲛ̄ matches the established formula in line 5.
